prompt: Hi! We need a proper data model for our new urban tree cadastre. The requirements doc and the dump of our legacy schema are attached. Target is PostgreSQL/PostGIS for the app, plus a JSON Schema for the monthly exchange file to the regional agency. I'm in meetings all day so I can't answer questions right now — please make sensible assumptions, write them down so I can check them later, and give me a complete first draft including the generated schemas. Put everything in a datamodel/ folder.
assertions: There is exactly one implementation-neutral source of truth for the model (no database-specific types in it), and the PostgreSQL DDL and JSON Schema are generated from it rather than written by hand in parallel
Assumptions and/or open questions are written to a file in datamodel/
Species is modelled as a managed, extensible code list or reference table rather than free text
Inspection records are protected from deletion and have an audit trail (who changed what, when)
Corrections of a tree's location are historised so the previous location and the correction time can be retrieved
Felled trees are kept with felling date and reason, and a felled tree can be linked to one or more replacement trees
The tree location is a PostGIS Point geometry with SRID 25832 and has a spatial (GiST) index, in the generated DDL or in a separate tuning script
Defects are modelled as multi-valued entries each with a severity (low/medium/high), not as comma-separated text
Expected volumes (trees, inspections per year, measures per year) are recorded per object type in the model, not only in prose
Inspector names are flagged as personal data and excluded from the open data export
The exchange file for the regional agency carries no inspector names (at most an internal or pseudonymous id)
The generated JSON Schema is a valid JSON Schema, and a realistic example exchange file validates against it
Each model element can be traced to its source (source IDs on the elements or a traceability table to requirements.md / legacy_trees.sql)

For tree species, the run checks for a standardised taxonomy or vocabulary (e.g. GBIF Backbone Taxonomy, World Flora Online) and either recommends reusing it, with a verifiable source and a fit assessment, or explains why the city's own species list is kept; it does not adopt a vocabulary silently
